name: section-helper
body:
A layout can render a section template directly with the `section` helper, exactly as if the instance had been written in Markdown: `{{ section "<name>" [fields] [body] [child…] }}`. `<name>` names a section-usage template; the call executes that template's own `layout.html.tmpl` and yields the same trusted HTML a Markdown-authored instance of the same template produces. `fields` is an optional map of source values (typically built with `dict`), validated like a section fence's YAML against the target's field schema (field-rules); when omitted, the target's defaults apply. `body` is an optional Markdown string, validated against the target's body rule (body-rules): a literal body string in the layout is checked with the rest of the template set at load (section-helper-load-checks), and a non-literal body expression is validated — and rejected — against the target's body rule at render/example time. Any arguments after `fields` and `body` are child sections passed to the target, each the result of a `child` constructor naming one of the target's declared `sections:` (its template chosen by an optional `template` key among its fields, child-constructor) or a `children` forwarding call naming one of the target's declared `sections:` (children-forwarding); the target renders those children exactly as authored child instances — the accepted-template check against its declared `sections:`, the declaration's min/max over the set passed, each child's field defaults and validation, each child's body rule, each child's own nested children, and each child's own `.item` descriptor — so a target that declares a mandatory child section is satisfied when the call passes the required children. The rendered instance is executed with the reserved `deck`/`slide` context and with an `.item` descriptor that treats it as a one-item group: `section` and `template` are the target name, `index` 0, `number` 1, `count` 1, `first` and `last` true, and `parent` is the calling instance's fields — the fields of the section instance whose layout made the call, or nil when the call is made from a slide layout. `.raw` carries the values the call supplied (raw-source-context). The target's own `.data.<child>` and rendered child-section lists are populated from the passed children, while the call itself adds nothing to the caller's `.data` or rendered section list (section-data-context). A `body` is the target's own body and carries no child sections: children pass only through child arguments, so a helper body whose heading names a declared child section of the target is rejected rather than silently dropped — at load for a literal body string (section-helper-load-checks), and at render/example time when a non-literal body is validated against the target's body rule.

AC: a slide layout calling `{{ section "footer" }}` renders the `footer` section template's HTML on the slide; `{{ section "number-heading" (dict "number" .item.number "heading" .raw.title) }}` renders that template with those field values; `{{ section "callout" (dict "label" "Proposition") .raw.body }}` renders `callout` with a literal field and the slide's original body as its body; `{{ section "columns" nil nil (child "column" (dict "title" "A")) (child "column" (dict "title" "B")) }}` renders `columns` with two `column` children, each reading its own `{{.item.index}}`/`{{.item.count}}`; `{{ section "columns" nil nil (children "column" .data.columns) }}` re-instantiates the caller's authored `column` entries as children; the rendered instance reads `{{.item.index}}`/`{{.item.number}}`/`{{.item.count}}`/`{{.item.first}}`/`{{.item.last}}` as 0/1/1/true/true, `{{.item.section}}`/`{{.item.template}}` as the target name, and `{{.item.parent.<field>}}` as the calling section instance's field (nil from a slide layout); the target reads `{{ len .data.columns }}` as its passed-child count.
